method: Checked out cursor/aud-0023-review-0db0 at tip a8795d62e (git reset --hard origin/...) with no prior exposure to the implementer's transcript. Read all three probe scripts (probe1_osv_scan.py, probe2_dependabot_alerts.py, detector_control.py) end-to-end before running anything, to understand exactly what each does (target discovery, osv-scanner invocation, GHSA dedup, gh api calls) rather than trusting the receipt's summary. Confirmed osv-scanner v1.9.2 and an authenticated gh CLI were available (installed to ~/go/bin, already on PATH). Re-ran all three named probes live from scratch. Then, independently of the receipt's own scripts, invoked osv-scanner myself with a hand-typed -L argument list (not calling probe1's find_targets()) and re-implemented the vuln-id/severity/package summarizer in a standalone Python snippet (not importing probe1_osv_scan.summarize) to rule out a shared bug producing the same wrong number twice. Independently called `gh api repos/Prekzursil/agent-skills-toolchain/dependabot/alerts --paginate` myself to confirm the 403 is real and not fabricated. Independently re-queried 5 of the 15 sampled Advisory-DB packages by hand and cross-checked the excluded 16th package (mcp, dropped only by the probe's SAMPLE_LIMIT=15 truncation) to check for sample cherry-picking. Investigated whether affected_package_count=21 is inflated by duplicate manifest paths (e.g. the documented skills/ vs .agents/skills/ compat-copy) by recomputing distinct (name,version) and distinct-name cardinalities from the raw affected_packages list. After running, git-diffed all touched probe output JSON files to confirm only started_at timestamps changed (byte-identical measured data), then `git checkout --` reverted those timestamp-only diffs to leave the review branch clean before writing this review artifact. Confirmed receipt state=BLOCKED and reviewer.verdict=NOT-REVIEWED remained untouched on disk throughout; did not modify the receipt.

falsification_attempts.attempt: Challenge whether affected_package_count=21 overclaims uniqueness, since the underlying list is built by appending one entry per (scanned-file, package) tuple without deduping across files -- and this repo has a documented compat-copy duplicate (skills/consensus-tooluniverse-research/requirements.txt is byte-identical to .agents/skills/consensus-tooluniverse-research/requirements.txt per AGENTS.md's migration-layer note), plus fast-uri==3.1.5 and qs==6.15.3 each appear in two separate npm projects (chrome-bridge-mcp and hacktricks-mcp-server package-lock.json files).
falsification_attempts.observed: Recomputing from the raw affected_packages list: distinct (name,version) pairs = 18, distinct package names = 16, but the receipt's own method field says 'osv-scanner packages with >=1 vulnerability' -- i.e. a raw count of osv-scanner's own per-source-file package-result entries, matching osv-scanner's native JSON grouping (results[].packages[], one row per scanned manifest). requests==2.31 is double-counted only because the compat-copy duplicate file genuinely exists twice on disk at two different repo paths (both would independently expose the pin if imported from either location); fast-uri and qs are double-counted because they are genuinely two separate npm projects each independently vulnerable, not the same exposure. The headline number is honestly reproducible and consistent with its documented counting method (occurrences, not distinct dependency identities); it is not fabricated, but a reader could reasonably want a 'distinct_affected_package_count=18' companion metric -- flagged below as a residual observation, not a broken headline claim.

falsification_attempts.attempt: Recompute the severity histogram sum (30+26+2=58) against distinct_vuln_id_count=77 to see if the two headline numbers are internally inconsistent (i.e. does the receipt imply severities sum to 77 when they demonstrably do not?).
falsification_attempts.observed: 34 of the 77 distinct vuln ids (mostly PYSEC-* PyPI advisories) carry no database_specific.severity field in osv-scanner's output at all, and the histogram counts per-package occurrences of a vuln id (not distinct ids), so sum(58) < distinct_vuln_id_count(77) is expected, not an error. The receipt's headline lists both numbers side-by-side but never asserts they sum to each other; re-verified this gap exists identically on my independent osv-scanner run, so it is a property of the underlying advisory data, not a probe artifact.

notes: Every headline count in the receipt reproduced exactly on a fresh live re-run of all three named probes, and -- more importantly -- on independently-written re-implementations that do not import the implementer's summarizer/comparator code (hand-typed osv-scanner target list + standalone dedup script for probe1; direct `gh api` calls bypassing probe2's helper functions). I specifically tried several distinct falsification angles: shared summarizer bug, fabricated 403, fabricated Advisory-DB counts, sample-cap cherry-picking (checked the one package the 15-cap silently excluded and found it would have corroborated too), inflated affected_package_count from the repo's documented skills/ vs .agents/skills/ duplicate file and cross-project duplicate npm packages, and an apparent severity-sum/vuln-id-count mismatch (58 vs 77, explained by 34 ids lacking a severity field). None of these broke a claimed headline number; the affected_package_count and severity-sum items are documented here as legitimate methodological nuances (occurrence-count vs distinct-identity; partial severity coverage) rather than falsifications, since the receipt's own method fields already describe the counting convention used and never claim the alternate interpretation. I did not promote the receipt; state=BLOCKED and reviewer.verdict=NOT-REVIEWED remain exactly as found on disk, and I reverted the timestamp-only diffs my probe re-runs produced before writing this review artifact so the branch stays clean. This independent-review.json is a separate artifact for a downstream packer step (not run by me) to consult when deciding whether to promote the receipt.
